Optimal.Notes: Cuphead runs at a rock-solid 60 fps at native resolution with a modest TDP; this is the recommended everyday profile for the best visual and gameplay experience.

profiles.Summary: Cuphead is a lightweight 2D hand-drawn action game that runs exceptionally well on the Steam Deck, easily hitting 60 fps at full resolution with minimal power draw. Its low PC requirements mean the Deck hardware is massively overpowered for it, resulting in excellent battery life across all profiles.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very low PC minimum requirements (circa-2008 GPU) and the Deck's RDNA 2 hardware. On your first run, confirm 60 fps is stable in the opening boss fight and reduce TDP further if battery life is the priority.

MaxBattery.Notes: A 4 W TDP and low GPU clock are more than enough for this 2D game at 30 fps. Battery life is exceptional; raise TDP if you notice any hitching during transitions.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The game is so light that Max Performance and Optimal are nearly identical; uncapping the GPU clock ensures zero hitching during scene loads or co-op sessions.

Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 at a locked 60 fps is the sweet spot — the game's hand-drawn animation was designed for 60 fps and looks its best here. A 6 W TDP cap keeps the Deck cool and quiet while maintaining a perfectly stable frame rate.

profiles.Summary: Cuphead is a lightweight 2D hand-drawn indie game with very low system requirements, running exceptionally well on the Steam Deck OLED at full resolution and high frame rates. It is Steam Deck Verified with a strong platinum ProtonDB rating, meaning virtually no compatibility issues are expected.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's very low PC requirements (circa-2008 GPU minimum) and the Deck hardware. On first run, confirm the frame rate is rock-solid at your chosen cap — if it ever dips, check that no background processes are interfering, as the game itself should never stress the Deck.

MaxBattery.Notes: Cuphead is extremely light on hardware; a 4 W TDP and low GPU clock are more than sufficient at 45 fps. This profile maximises session length while remaining very smooth for a 2D action game.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The OLED's 90 Hz panel and Cuphead's minimal GPU demand make a locked 90 fps easily achievable; the 10 W TDP cap is generous headroom — the game will rarely use it. Note that Cuphead's animation is hand-drawn at a fixed cadence, so visual benefit above 60 fps is subtle but input latency improves.
